issues.legal_issue: A grant conferring control over land and entitlement to its revenue constitutes an estate interest that is extinguished and vested in the State when the land-reform law takes effect.
material_facts: A hereditary grant covered 41 villages and was made to provide income for worship at a temple.
The grant entitled its holders to take possession of and control the lands, collect land revenue from the zamindars, and use the proceeds for worship.
The grant described the land and its increases as free from government demands, and the holders and their descendants collected the revenue over time.
The holder also acquired some zamindari rights through purchases in execution of decrees; compensation by annuity was paid for those rights, but the disputed jagirdari rights were not recognized.
The holder sought judicial relief requiring recognition and enforcement of the jagirdari rights, and appealed after that relief was denied.
issues.conclusion: The grant conferred an interest in land constituting an estate, not merely a right to a fixed pension. Under the combined operation of sections 4 and 6, the jagirdari rights ceased and vested in the State free from encumbrances; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The scheme of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 was to extinguish estates, derivative rights in estates, and the interests of intermediaries between the State and the tiller of the soil. Under section 3(8), read with section 3(26), the grant constituted an estate; section 4 provided for estates to vest in the State, and section 6 provided that intermediaries' rights and grants or confirmations of title to land or rights in respect of land or its revenue would cease or determine. The Court followed State of Uttar Pradesh v. Kunwar Sri Trivikram Narain Singh, [1962] 3 SCR 213.

predicates.appeal_challenges_denial_of_recognition: A person appeals after a court denies relief sought to obtain recognition or enforcement of jagirdari rights.
predicates.grant_conferred_interest_in_land: A grant gives its holder possession or control of land and an entitlement to collect or use its revenue, rather than only a fixed payment.
predicates.jagirdari_rights_existed_when_vesting_to: The jagirdari rights remained in existence when the land-acquisition scheme took effect.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns denial of recognition of existing jagirdari rights arising from a grant of an interest in land, those rights cease and vest in the State.
